messages.content:
The failing test `testOptionGroupLong` is trying to select an option from an `OptionGroup` in Apache Commons CLI library. The test adds two options to the group, one with a long name "foo" and the other with a long name "bar". When parsing the command line with the argument "--bar", it expects the "bar" option to be selected in the group.

The current bug report describes that when an option in the group has a long name but no short name, setting the selected option using `group.setSelected(option)` has no effect.

By looking at the implementation of the `org.apache.commons.cli.OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` method, we see that it checks if an option has been selected previously, and if not, it sets the selected option based on the provided option's short name.

However, in the `OptionBuilder.create(String opt)` method, which is used to create options with long names, there is no provision to set a short name for the option being created. This means that the options created with `OptionBuilder.withLongOpt("foo").create()` and `OptionBuilder.withLongOpt("bar").create()` in the test have no short names assigned to them.

Therefore, when trying to set the selected option using `group.setSelected(option)` in the test, the method cannot effectively determine the selected option because it relies on checking the short name of the option, which is not set for options created with long names only.

To fix this issue, the `OptionBuilder.create(String opt)` method should be modified to also allow specifying a short name for the option being created, or the `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` method should be updated to handle options without short names properly.

The likely locations to be fixed are:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.OptionBuilder.create(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.cli.OptionGroup.setSelected(org.apache.commons.cli.Option)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
